transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Eleanor Wu (Clearhaven CTO), Samir Khan (Clearhaven Platform Eng), Lara Price (Clearhaven ML Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough):
Clearhaven is evaluating Redwood for a PoC focused on low p95 latency for streaming responses and steady token/sec throughput at 12-16 concurrent sessions. Primary constraints: data residency in EU, SOC2 audit, and an internal SLA requiring p95 < 350ms for 256-token responses. They want a short baseline run and a recommended config (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with cost/latency tradeoffs.

Topics discussed:
- p95 targets and how Redwood measures p95 (server-side vs end-to-end)
- concurrency profiles and sustained token/sec vs burst characteristics
- streaming vs non-streaming impact on latency and CPU/GPU utilization
- Dedicated pools and private (VPC/on-prem) deployment implications for SLOs and compliance
- benchmarking approach and artifacts to share

Action items (recapped here, also in metadata):
- Redwood will deliver a runbook + benchmarking script
- Clearhaven to provide prompts and sample load traces
- Schedule a follow-up technical deep dive with infra + security

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription may contain errors and mis-hearings):
00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood here, I'll kick off and Diego our SE will jump into the nitty gritty in the middle. Can you each say quick hi?
00:12 Eleanor Wu: Hi, Eleanor here — CTO at Clearhaven. Thanks, Maya.
00:16 Samir Khan: Samir — platform, hello.
00:19 Lara Price: Lara, ML eng, hi.
00:23 Maya Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda: make sure we understand your p95 and concurrency goals, go over what we mean by hosted/dedicated/private in practice, and then agree on next steps for a baseline run. Does that sound right?
00:33 Eleanor Wu: Yep, that's right. We're time boxed here — legal wants the compliance check by end of month but technical approves PoC first.
00:38 Diego Morales: Cool. Just quick framing — when you say p95, are you measuring from client receive to streaming first token or server-side generation time? That changes numbers by 50-200ms depending on network.
00:47 Samir Khan: Good call. Our SLO is end-to-end p95 from client request to first token received. We run users in EU, so region matters.
00:55 Diego Morales: Perfect, we typically separate server p95 and client p95 in all our docs. For hosted, Redwood provides region pinned endpoints EU-west, so network overhead will be minimal but you should still expect some variability. For dedicated we can get you more consistent server-side p95 since it's reserved GPUs.
01:10 Lara Price: Our initial target is p95 <= 350ms for 256-token responses with streaming first-token under 120ms ideally. We don't want interactive chatter to be laggy.
01:20 Maya Patel: That's a tight but reasonable goal. Quick clarify — 256-token response, is that typical for chat completions or longer-multiturn summarizations?
01:27 Lara Price: Most are chat style, but about 20% are longer summaries. For bench we'll start with the chat pattern.
01:31 Diego Morales: Ok. For that workload the two variables you'll hit are model selection and batching. If you prefer lower latency at steady concurrency of 12-16 sessions, we often recommend the smaller 7B-ish variants quantized, or an optimized fp16 on dedicated for lower p95.
01:46 Eleanor Wu: We're actually evaluating both open-weights and a license model. We can't open-source certain prompts due to PII, so data residency and KMS integration matter.
01:55 Maya Patel: Understood. For KMS we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in the private deployment. Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but we can do VPC + bring-your-own-key for Dedicated if needed.
02:07 Samir Khan: How about burst behavior — we have periodic bursts up to 40 concurrent short chats for campaign spikes. Will Redwood throttle or queue?
02:16 Diego Morales: That depends on plan and policy. Hosted will enforce rate limits per account which can be raised; dedicated gives you reserved throughput and predictable queueing. Private you control autoscaling but you also control costs. For burst smoothing we have smart routing and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if latency spikes but you can opt-out.
02:34 Lara Price: Walk us through what a baseline benchmark looks like. We want reproducible scripts and end-to-end numbers.
02:40 Maya Patel: We'll share a runbook with a JMeter-style script and a small Redwood load harness that runs streaming sessions with realistic token distributions. Step 1 is synthetic: 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16 concurrency ramps. Step 2 is representative prompts you provide. We'll record both server and client p95, token/sec, and GPU utilization.
02:58 Diego Morales: One note: streaming increases CPU and network overhead because of chunking — you might see slightly higher server-side p95 for first token but better user-perceived latency for the rest. Also KV cache warmup matters for repeated prefixes — if you have a lot of repeated context we can shave 20-40% of token cost.
03:15 Samir Khan: You mentioned KV cash?
03:17 Diego Morales: Sorry, K-V cache — sometimes transcription has me saying "cash" but yes K-V cache.
03:23 Eleanor Wu: For compliance, SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves. Do you provide immutable audit logs and identity bindings?
03:30 Maya Patel: Yes — hosted provides audit logs and SSO/SAML integration. Private gives you full control and deeper audit retention. We can share our SOC2 report and an architecture note on how audit logs are stored.
03:42 Lara Price: For the PoC, what are quick win configs? Hosted with larger model or dedicated with smaller optimized model?
03:49 Diego Morales: Tradeoff — hosted with a beefy model (e.g., 13B fp16) might give better accuracy but variability in p95. Dedicated with an optimized 7B quantized model often gives lower p95 and is cheaper per token if you have sustained load. For your 12-16 sustained concurrency plus 40-concurrent bursts, dedicated is a predictable bet.
04:05 Maya Patel: We can also propose a hybrid: start hosted to iterate quickly, then shift the heavy steady-state to dedicated with a canary for fallbacks. That reduces time-to-value while ensuring SLOs for production.
04:16 Samir Khan: Cost concerns — approximate monthly cost for Dedicated? Ballpark numbers are fine.
04:20 Maya Patel: For reserved Dedicated the pricing varies by pool size and GPU type. As a rough example, a small 4-GPU pool for steady 16 concurrency might be X per month — I'll include a ballpark sheet in the runbook. Hosted per-token costs will be higher at scale.
04:33 Lara Price: Are there known regressions in streaming vs non-streaming for output coherence?
04:37 Diego Morales: Generally not. Streaming is just how tokens are delivered. If you do function calling or structured outputs, latency for first token matters more; but content quality shouldn't degrade. Sometimes truncation in chunk sizes can add small artifacts but rare.
04:51 Eleanor Wu: From an infra perspective, can you expose Prometheus metrics and traces? We want to fold Redwood metrics into our observability.
04:57 Diego Morales: Yes, Dedicated and Private support Prometheus export and traces (open-telemetry). Hosted has a limited metrics API but we can provide aggregated telemetry and traces on request under enterprise agreements.
05:10 Lara Price: On concurrency, how do you handle KV cache eviction under many unique sessions? Our user sessions have diverse contexts.
05:17 Diego Morales: If you have very high context variance, the KV cache hit rate drops and you'll see higher per-token compute. For that pattern, we recommend batch size tuning, smaller sequence lengths, and possibly dynamic caching policies. We can run a heatmap analysis in the PoC.
05:30 Samir Khan: Let's talk measurement specifics. For p95 < 350ms we need a repeatable profiling harness. Will you instrument network latency separately?
05:36 Maya Patel: Yes, our runbook includes client-side synthetic runner that records FIRST_BYTE time and server-side generation timestamp. We'll share the exact instrumentation hooks.
05:44 Diego Morales: Also worth calling out cold-starts — if you're on a low-util dedicated node and it scales from zero you may see cold p95 outliers. We'll recommend always-on for a reserved pool or warmers for predictable p95.
05:58 Eleanor Wu: We might be constrained by our procurement timeline — if dedicated setup requires contract lead time of 4–6 weeks that might slip our internal calendar.
06:06 Maya Patel: We understand. Hosted gives the fastest spin-up; Dedicated can be pre-provisioned if you want to lock a pilot. We'll flag procurement in the next steps.
06:15 Lara Price: Can you also run a token/sec ceiling test? We want sustained throughput numbers for streaming and non-streaming under 1 minute windows.
06:22 Diego Morales: Yes, we'll do sustained token/sec and peak token/sec tests. Typical measurement: tokens/s on GPU (server-side) and token output/s client-side including network. We'll show both.
06:32 Samir Khan: Anything about quantization we should worry about for accuracy?
06:36 Diego Morales: For many models, 4-bit quantization is nearly lossless for many tasks but it depends on your eval. We'll include a quick quantization quality report in the deliverables.
06:46 Maya Patel: Quick check — do you have any hard constraints on region or VPC? Eleanor?
06:51 Eleanor Wu: EU-only data residency for production. For PoC we can run in EU but have dev teams in US that might test.
06:59 Diego Morales: We can pin to EU region endpoints for hosted and deploy Dedicated within EU if you want. Private on-prem is also an option later if audits require it.
07:09 Lara Price: One operational question — when a model variant is falling back or degraded, how does Redwood surface that? We need clear signals to our app.
07:17 Maya Patel: We emit structured error codes and a fallback header in responses. Console has per-route degradation graphs and alerts; we can also provide webhook hooks to your orchestration.
07:26 Samir Khan: Will you be able to share your latency vs concurrency S-curves? That helps us decide the autoscale points.
07:31 Diego Morales: Yes — we'll include S-curve plots from our runs and suggested autoscale breakpoints.
07:36 Lara Price: Ok, let's get concrete about the initial benchmark matrix.
07:39 Maya Patel: Proposed matrix: model variant (7B-quant, 7B-fp16, 13B-fp16), load sweep (1,2,4,8,12,16 sustained), burst tests (40,60 concurrent for 30s), streaming vs non-streaming, 256-token and 512-token response sizes. Does that cover it?
07:57 Eleanor Wu: Yes. Also add a 1% request with 6k context to see long-term cost behavior.
08:03 Diego Morales: Good call. We'll also capture GPU util and per-token ms.
08:08 Maya Patel: Next steps recap then: I will send the runbook + benchmarking harness by Tuesday (2026-08-25), Diego will run an internal sim and attach a sample S-curve, Lara will send prompt set + logs by Sunday (2026-08-23), and we'll schedule a technical deep dive week of 2026-08-31. Anything else?
08:27 Eleanor Wu: Can you also include a short note on expected monthly cost ranges for dedicated vs hosted for our scale?
08:33 Maya Patel: Yes, I'll include a cost worksheet with assumptions and floor/ceiling.
08:36 Samir Khan: One small thing — our security team wants to see audit log retention options (30/90/365 days).
08:41 Maya Patel: We'll include retention tiers and how Private can give you longer retention.
08:45 Lara Price: Great. Thanks, this was helpful.
08:48 Maya Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up via email with artifacts.

End of call.

Notes about transcription quality: speaker overlaps occasionally (e.g., 01:17), product names sometimes mis-transcribed: "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Redwood Dedicated. Several timestamps are rounded to nearest 5–10 seconds.
